probes.note: 🔴 AC-1 probe 1b, the one PLAN-0120 declared and s277 never ran. Stops db_support reading the role, so the CHILD resolves an unsuffixed name and exits 3. probes.name: P1c
probes.subject: .claude/hooks/_goal_gate.py
probes.note: 🔴 The tail is carried at all. Same shape as s277's G2 on the sibling test. state == CHECK_PASS stays GREEN here — that green is what rules out 'something unrelated broke'.

probes.name: P2
probes.subject: tests/db_support.py
probes.note: 🔴 AC-2's declared probe: the suffix becomes unconditional. PLAN-0120 predicted this reddens the `name_without == parent` equality and leaves the inequality green. Code's s278 analysis says the REVERSE — parent, injected child and un-injected child all resolve `..._gate`, so the two names coincide (inequality reddens) while both still equal the parent (equality stays green). This probe measures which is true.

exemptions.test_the_check_child_resolves_a_gate_sco: 🟢 Co-falsified with `state == CHECK_PASS` under P1b and NOT-REACHED after it: the child's exit code IS derived from the suffix check, so the two assertions read one fact two ways and no mutation separates them. Its independent content — that the tail carries a readable name at all — is witnessed by P1c on the helper's count assert.
exemptions.test_without_injection_the_child_name_eq: 🟢 A co-moving AGREEMENT claim: parent and un-injected child run the identical resolution code (tests/db_support.py at import), so any single source mutation moves BOTH sides and the equality survives it. That is the handoff's 'an assertion compared against a value that moves with the mutation has no witness' shape, recorded rather than papered over. Its hazard content — that an un-injected child is NOT isolated from this session — is what `name_with != name_without` asserts, and P2 reddens that.
